about.title: Atwater Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone you love in a traffic collision is a weight no family should carry alone, and in Atwater the burden often falls on households already stretched thin. Merced County recorded one traffic death alongside dozens of injury collisions in the most recent year, a reminder that Atwater's mix of local roads and SR-99 traffic carries real consequences for families here. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs able to step in when no immediate family remains. These claims exist separately from any criminal proceedings connected to the crash, and they can help a family recover funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's companionship and guidance. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can walk through your specific situation and explain what's possible under California law.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people — spouses, domestic partners, and children first, then other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help clarify where your family stands before any paperwork is filed.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Window
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, and that window can be shorter if a government entity was involved, such as a public road defect. Missing this deadline can permanently close the door on a claim.

items.title: Losses Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California can account for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the family would have received, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — not just immediate expenses.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim after a crash in Atwater?
items.answer: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, that deadline is often much shorter, sometimes just months. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure this window isn't missed.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California law prioritizes a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children as the people who can file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the family's circumstances. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and explain where you fit.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim depend on criminal charges being filed against the other driver?
items.answer: No — a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case tied to a fatal collision on roads like Shaffer Road or SR-99. Charges may or may not be filed by prosecutors, but that decision doesn't determine whether your family can pursue a civil claim. The two processes run independently under California law.

items.question: What costs can a wrongful death claim help with?
items.answer: These claims can address funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their companionship and guidance. Every family's losses look different, so it helps to discuss your specific circumstances with an attorney.
